3-month-cloud-computing.summary: Three months that take you from your first terminal command to a real AWS deployment you can show in an interview — Linux, Bash, networking and Git from the ground up, then hands-on AWS services. No programming experience needed.
overview: This is the 3-month Cloud Computing program at techcadd in {city}, for students who have just completed 12th from any stream. It starts from scratch — Linux, Bash scripting and networking are taught from the very basics, so no prior coding or technical background is needed. Once the fundamentals are clear, you move into a real AWS account and work hands-on with core services: IAM, VPC, EC2, S3, RDS and Auto Scaling.

Every topic ends with something you actually build — a script, a secure network, a hosted web application. These add up across the three months to a scalable cloud architecture capstone with an architecture diagram and documentation, work you can show in interviews for roles like Cloud Support Engineer or AWS Cloud Trainee.
3-month-cloud-computing.syllabusIntro: The course is divided into three months. Each month builds on the previous one, moving from basics to real AWS projects.

modules.title: Month 1 — Foundations: Linux, Scripting, Networking & Git
points: Linux basics — installation, file system, commands for navigation, file management, searching and archiving; text editors (vi/vim, nano); redirection, pipes and filters.
Users, groups, permissions, sudo; package management (apt, yum); process and service management with systemd; SSH remote access and cron scheduling.
Bash scripting — variables, conditionals (if/case), loops (for/while), functions; writing backup, log-rotation and health-check scripts.
Computer networking — LAN, WAN, routers, switches, firewalls; OSI and TCP/IP models; IP addressing, subnetting, DNS, DHCP and NAT.
TCP vs UDP, HTTP/HTTPS basics; troubleshooting with ping, traceroute, dig, netstat and curl.
Git and GitHub — repositories, commits, branches, merging and pull requests; .gitignore; GitHub Actions basics for automation.
Tools covered: Linux (Ubuntu / Amazon Linux) · Bash · SSH · Git · GitHub · Wireshark
Projects: Linux administration lab + Bash automation toolkit (backup, log parser, health-check scripts) + networking troubleshooting report.

modules.title: Month 2 — Core AWS: Cloud Concepts, IAM, VPC, EC2 & Security
points: What is cloud computing — on-premises vs cloud, IaaS / PaaS / SaaS with examples; AWS shared responsibility model; benefits and real-world use cases.
AWS global infrastructure — regions, availability zones and edge locations; the AWS Console, CLI and free tier; account setup with billing alarms and budgets.
IAM (Identity & Access Management) — users, groups, roles and policies; least-privilege access; MFA setup; CloudTrail for tracking activity.
VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) — creating a VPC with public and private subnets; route tables, internet gateway and NAT gateway; security groups and network ACLs.
EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) — launching instances, key pairs, SSH access; Amazon Machine Images (AMIs); EBS storage, snapshots and encryption.
Installing a web server (Nginx/Apache) on EC2; deploying a simple web application; understanding instance types and pricing options.
Tools covered: AWS Console · AWS CLI · IAM · CloudTrail · VPC · EC2 · EBS · Nginx / Apache
Projects: Secure AWS network (VPC with subnets, NAT, security groups) + web application hosted on EC2.

modules.title: Month 3 — Storage, Databases, Scaling & Capstone Project
points: Amazon S3 — buckets, objects, storage classes, lifecycle policies; static website hosting; bucket policies and encryption; versioning.
Amazon RDS — relational databases on AWS, supported engines, backups and snapshots; connecting an application to RDS securely.
DynamoDB basics — tables, keys, capacity modes; choosing between relational and non-relational databases for different use cases.
Load balancing and auto scaling — Application Load Balancer (ALB), target groups and health checks; Auto Scaling groups and scaling policies.
Route 53 for DNS management; CloudWatch for monitoring, alarms and dashboards; introduction to the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
Capstone project — build a complete application using EC2, VPC, S3, RDS, load balancer and CloudWatch; architecture diagram, documentation, presentation and mock interview.
Tools covered: S3 · RDS · DynamoDB · ALB · Auto Scaling · Route 53 · CloudWatch
Projects: S3 static website + RDS-backed application + scalable cloud architecture capstone with documentation.

3-month-flutter.summary: Three months that take you from your first line of Dart to a production-signed app on the store — widgets, state, live data, Firebase, tests and a custom UI, built on real devices. No programming experience needed.
overview: Dart is taught first — syntax, OOP, collections and null safety — before a single widget, then you move into building real apps: layouts, state management with Provider and Bloc, REST APIs, Firebase authentication and Firestore, and automated testing. Every topic ends with something you build and can show, closing with a production-signed app carrying a deployed store listing and a technical handoff report — the kind of proof Junior Flutter Developer and Cross-Platform UI Developer interviews ask for.

3-month-mern-stack.summary: A fast-paced three-month programme taking you from web fundamentals to a complete, deployed MERN stack application with authentication, database integration and placement guidance.
overview: This is the three-month MERN Stack program at techcadd in {city} — beginner to intermediate, written for someone starting straight after 12th who wants a deployed full-stack application quickly rather than the longest possible syllabus. It runs three or more mini projects plus one industry-level major project, and is fast-paced by design: each month carries a single theme, which is what lets a student finish with something live inside a single term.

Month one covers web development fundamentals and JavaScript: how the internet works, client–server architecture, frontend versus backend versus full stack, HTTP/HTTPS, domains and hosting; HTML5 structure, semantic tags, forms, tables, media and accessibility; CSS3 selectors, the box model, Flexbox, Grid, animations, responsive design and media queries; JavaScript from variables and loops through ES6+, DOM manipulation, event handling, async JavaScript, the Fetch API and local storage; and Git and GitHub. The month produces five small builds — a portfolio website, a calculator, a to-do list, a weather app and a responsive landing page.

Month two moves into React.js and MongoDB: React fundamentals with Vite, JSX, components, props and state; event handling, conditional rendering, lists and keys, forms, the useState and useEffect hooks and API integration; React Router DOM, protected routes, the Context API and Tailwind CSS; then MongoDB fundamentals and Atlas, collections and documents, CRUD and query operators, and Mongoose for connecting Node.js to MongoDB with schemas, models and validation. The mini projects here are a blog application, an employee dashboard and a student management system backed by a real database.

3-month-agentic-ai.summary: Three months that take you from your first line of Python to an autonomous agent running in public, with citations, guardrails and a cost-per-conversation figure behind it. No programming experience needed.
overview: This is the 3-month Agentic AI program at techcadd in {city}, built for students who have just finished 12th from any stream, with no prior coding experience required. A language model answers a question; an agent decides what to do next — it plans, calls real tools, reads what comes back, and repeats until the goal is met. The course teaches you to build, test and deploy these AI agents from scratch.

It starts from the basics — Python, the command line, Git, HTTP and databases — before moving into agent engineering: prompting, tool calling, retrieval-augmented generation, memory and deployment. Every topic ends with a project you build yourself, from a published MCP server to a cited RAG assistant, closing with a publicly deployed agent as the capstone — the kind of proof that AI Automation Engineer and Agentic AI Developer interviews ask for.
3-month-agentic-ai.syllabusIntro: The course is divided into three months. Each month builds on the previous one, moving from basics to deploying a real AI agent.

Agent frameworks — LangGraph nodes, edges, conditional routing, cycles and subgraphs; typed state and streaming.
Human-in-the-loop — approval gates, time-travel debugging, durable execution and resumability.
Multi-agent patterns — supervisor and worker roles, the handoff pattern, termination conditions.

Projects: Cited compliance copilot (RAG with 0.85+ faithfulness) + multi-tenant memory layer + stateful approval agent with checkpointing.

4-month-digital-marketing.summary: Own every source of traffic on Google — rank organically, buy intelligently, and prove results with data. Four months covering both search engines plus a Meta retargeting layer, finishing with 14 globally recognised certifications and a 30-day growth sprint on a live business.
overview: techcadd's 4-Month SEO + Performance Marketing programme in {city} is built on a simple premise: a business gets traffic from Google in two ways — by ranking for it and by buying it — and the professionals agencies value most understand both rather than half the picture. The course runs for four months across 170+ contact hours of classroom and supervised lab time, open to anyone from 10+2 onward, including graduates and working professionals, with a beginner-to-full-search-marketer level and a mix of practical lab work and the theory behind it. On top of the two Google traffic engines sits a Meta retargeting layer and a full measurement stack, all tied to 14 certification exams, 6 portfolio projects and a 30-day integrated growth sprint on a live business.

Months one and two build the organic engine: funnel architecture, buyer personas, competitor teardowns and the metrics vocabulary of the job (CPM, CPC, CTR, CPL, CAC, AOV, LTV, ROAS, ROI), then keyword research and search intent classification, on-page SEO, and technical SEO covering crawl budget, canonicals, hreflang, Core Web Vitals and structured data. From there the course adds off-page link building and digital PR, local SEO and Google Business Profile, and content marketing and conversion copywriting, closing month two with a timed live SEO audit as the mid-term practical. Month three is the whole of Google Ads rather than a Search-only sample — account architecture, auction mechanics, Quality Score and Responsive Search Ads on the Search and Display side, then Shopping, Performance Max and YouTube with Merchant Center feeds and audience signals. Month four adds Meta Ads (Business Manager, Pixel installation, the Conversions API, audience and retargeting strategy, Advantage+ Shopping), GA4, Google Tag Manager and Looker Studio for measurement, and closes on media buying economics — break-even ROAS, attribution and blended versus platform ROAS.

Each stage is tied to a project you keep, not just a topic covered in class: a combined organic-and-paid search strategy document, an on-page and technical SEO overhaul with the fixes actually implemented and Core Web Vitals re-measured afterwards, a full Google Ads account build spanning Search, Display and Performance Max with a Merchant Center feed, a Meta retargeting layer with Pixel and Conversions API in place, and a unified Looker Studio dashboard blending Search Console, GA4, Google Ads and Meta Ads. These feed into the capstone — a 30-day integrated growth sprint where organic and paid work run together on a real partner business, reviewed weekly by a mentor, ending in a board-style presentation.

overview: This is the three-month AI-Powered Cybersecurity program at techcadd in {city}, built for someone starting straight after 12th who wants working security skills quickly rather than the longest possible syllabus. It is fast-paced by design — each month carries a single theme — and the pace is what lets a student finish with a working AI security tool inside one term, with a set of mini projects marking the end of every month.

Month one covers cybersecurity, networking and system administration. It opens with cybersecurity fundamentals — the CIA triad, security domains, types of cyber attack, career paths, cyber laws and ethics — then computer hardware and operating systems, Windows and Linux administration, user and group management and file system permissions. overview: techcadd's 6-Month Cloud Computing programme in {city} is a complete course for students who have just finished 12th, with no prior coding or IT background required. It starts at the very beginning — what a server is, how Linux works, how computers talk to each other over a network — and works up to hosting, securing and automating applications on AWS, practised the same day in a live, licensed AWS account under trainer supervision. Classes run 2 hours a day across six months, ending in a certificate and placement support.

The six months are laid out month by month: Linux, basic scripting, networking and Git; cloud basics and core AWS services — IAM, VPC and EC2; storage, databases, load balancing, Auto Scaling and monitoring with S3, RDS, DynamoDB and CloudWatch; serverless AWS, AWS AI services and cloud security with Lambda, API Gateway, KMS and GuardDuty; Docker containers and Kubernetes, including EKS and Helm; and finally CI/CD automation with Jenkins, infrastructure as code with Terraform, and monitoring with Prometheus and Grafana.

Each month closes with a project: a Linux and Bash automation toolkit, a secure AWS network with a live web server, a scalable multi-tier cloud application, a serverless workflow with an AI chatbot, a containerised application on Kubernetes, and an automated deployment pipeline with Terraform-managed infrastructure — six pieces of work for a portfolio rather than one certificate.
6-month-cloud-computing.syllabusIntro: The course runs month by month. Each month lists what you learn, the tools you use and the project you finish it with — moving from basics to a complete, running cloud system.

modules.title: Month 1 — Linux, Basic Scripting, Networking & Git
points: Linux basics — installing it, understanding the file system, moving around with commands, creating and managing files, searching, and using text editors (nano, vi).
Users, groups and permissions; installing software with package managers; starting and stopping services; connecting to a remote machine with SSH; scheduling automatic tasks with cron.
Bash scripting for beginners — variables, if-conditions, loops and small functions; writing simple scripts that take backups, clean up logs and check whether a server is healthy.
How networks work — routers, switches and firewalls; IP addresses and subnetting; DNS (how a website name becomes an address); DHCP and NAT explained simply.
TCP and UDP, HTTP and HTTPS; finding network problems using ping, traceroute, dig, netstat and curl.
Git and GitHub — saving versions of your work, commits, branches, merging and pull requests, so all your later projects are stored properly.
Tools used: Linux (Ubuntu / Amazon Linux) · Bash · SSH · cron · Git · GitHub
Project: a Linux administration lab plus a small automation toolkit — backup, log-cleaning and health-check scripts stored on GitHub.

modules.title: Month 2 — Cloud Basics & Core AWS: IAM, VPC and EC2
points: What cloud computing actually is — your own servers versus rented ones; IaaS, PaaS and SaaS explained with everyday examples; who is responsible for what between you and AWS.

How AWS is organised worldwide — regions, availability zones and edge locations; using the AWS Console and the AWS CLI; creating an account with the free tier, billing alarms and a budget so costs never surprise you.
IAM (Identity and Access Management) — creating users, groups, roles and permission policies; giving people only the access they need; turning on MFA; tracking who did what with CloudTrail.

VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) — building your own private network on AWS with public and private subnets, route tables, an internet gateway and a NAT gateway; protecting it with security groups and network ACLs.
EC2 (virtual servers) — launching an instance, using key pairs, connecting over SSH, choosing machine images and instance sizes, attaching EBS storage, taking snapshots and encrypting them.
Installing a web server (Nginx or Apache) on EC2 and putting a working website online; understanding pricing options so you can pick the cheapest sensible one.
Tools used: AWS Console · AWS CLI · IAM · CloudTrail · VPC · EC2 · EBS · Nginx / Apache
Project: a secure AWS network of your own, with a live website running on an EC2 server inside it.

modules.title: Month 3 — Storage, Databases, Auto Scaling & Monitoring
points: Amazon S3 — buckets and objects, storage classes and lifecycle rules, hosting a static website, bucket policies, versioning and encryption.
Amazon RDS — running a managed database on AWS, automatic backups and snapshots, and connecting an application to it securely.
DynamoDB basics — tables, keys and capacity; when a normal (relational) database is the right choice and when it is not.
Load balancing with an Application Load Balancer — target groups and health checks — so traffic is shared across servers and a failed server is taken out automatically.
Auto Scaling — adding servers automatically when traffic rises and removing them when it falls, so the site stays up without wasting money.
Route 53 for domain names and DNS; CloudWatch for monitoring, alarms and dashboards; an introduction to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, the checklist AWS itself uses for good design.
Tools used: S3 · RDS · DynamoDB · Application Load Balancer · Auto Scaling · Route 53 · CloudWatch
Project: a scalable, multi-tier web application using EC2, S3, RDS, a load balancer and Auto Scaling, with monitoring dashboards and an architecture diagram.

modules.title: Month 4 — Serverless AWS, AI Services & Cloud Security
points: Serverless computing — running code without managing any server at all. AWS Lambda functions, memory and timeout settings, and exposing them to the internet with API Gateway.
Connecting services into automatic workflows using EventBridge, SNS notifications and SQS queues, including dead-letter queues for messages that fail.
Writing your infrastructure as a file with CloudFormation, so a whole environment can be created, updated or deleted the same way every time.

Using AWS AI services in a simple, practical way — Amazon Bedrock for chat and text generation, Rekognition for images, Textract for reading documents and Comprehend for understanding text — called from Python with a small Streamlit interface.
Cloud security — hardening IAM, encrypting data at rest and in transit, managing keys with KMS, and keeping passwords out of your code using Secrets Manager and Parameter Store.
Protecting a website with ACM certificates, AWS WAF and Shield; spotting suspicious activity with GuardDuty; backups with AWS Backup and a written, tested disaster-recovery plan.
Tools used: Lambda · API Gateway · EventBridge · SNS · SQS · CloudFormation · Bedrock · Rekognition · Textract · Python · Streamlit · KMS · Secrets Manager · WAF · GuardDuty · AWS Backup
Project: an event-driven serverless workflow plus a small AI-powered chatbot on AWS, with security hardening applied and a backup and recovery plan documented.

modules.title: Month 5 — Docker Containers & Kubernetes
points: What containers are and why they replaced "it works on my machine" — containers compared with virtual machines, and how Docker is put together.
Writing a Dockerfile step by step; building images, tagging and versioning them; keeping images small with multi-stage builds; running, inspecting and debugging containers.

Storing data with volumes; connecting containers over Docker networks; running a multi-container application with Docker Compose; pushing images to Docker Hub and Amazon ECR; scanning images for known security problems.
Why orchestration is needed once you have many containers, and how a Kubernetes cluster is arranged, in plain terms.

Early months build core agent skills — data pipelines, retrieval, memory and multi-agent coordination, also covered on the shorter 3-month and 6-month programs — and later months revisit the same domains at production depth: an ingestion backbone with permission-aware retrieval, a twenty-million-document index, cross-organisation A2A protocols, an evaluation service, post-training with fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, voice and multimodal agents, and a governance layer mapped to the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

9-month-agentic-ai.syllabusIntro: Nine months of hands-on learning, organised month by month. Each month names its topics, the tools used in labs and the project you finish it with.

modules.title: Month 1 — Data Engineering & Knowledge Pipelines
points: Source connectors and change-data-capture across Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, document management systems and the warehouse.
Incremental, resumable and idempotent ingestion; document normalisation and layout-aware parsing at volume; deduplication and near-duplicate detection.
ACL and permission propagation from source system to index; PII classification at ingest.
Data contracts, schema evolution and lineage; backfill and full-reindex strategies; freshness SLAs and staleness detection.
Tool stack: Dagster · Airflow · Debezium · dbt · Docling · Unstructured · Iceberg · Delta · Kafka · Presidio · OpenLineage · DuckDB
Real use: a permission-faithful ingestion backbone — twenty source systems feeding one index nightly, where a document a user cannot open in SharePoint is a document their agent cannot retrieve.
Deliverable: incremental CDC ingestion pipeline with ACL propagation, lineage tracking, PII tagging, a backfill runbook and a freshness SLA dashboard.

modules.title: Month 2 — Retrieval at Scale & Vector Infrastructure
points: Embedding model selection and domain adaptation; ANN index internals — HNSW, IVF-PQ, DiskANN — and their recall, latency and memory trade-offs.
Sharding, replication and billion-scale design; multi-tenancy and row-level security in vector stores.
Document AI for tables, forms and scans; multimodal embeddings; retrieval cost modelling.
Index rebuild and migration without downtime.
Real use: an enterprise knowledge substrate — twenty million documents indexed on the ingestion pipeline, permission-filtered per user and queryable in under 300 milliseconds at the 95th percentile.
Deliverable: scalable retrieval platform with permission-aware filtering and a recall and latency benchmark across three index configurations.

modules.title: Month 3 — GraphRAG, Knowledge Graphs & Agentic Retrieval
points: Query planning and decomposition; knowledge-graph construction — entity and relation extraction, ontology design, community detection, global versus local queries.
Corrective and self-RAG loops; agentic retrieval where the agent plans its own searches.
Structured-data agents with text-to-SQL, schema grounding and guardrails; retrieval error analysis at scale.
Tool stack: Neo4j · Cypher · Microsoft GraphRAG · Graphiti · LightRAG · LlamaIndex Workflows · RAGatouille · Vanna · RAGAS

Real use: risk and exposure analysis. Answering "what is our total exposure to this counterparty across all entities, contracts and jurisdictions?" requires traversing relationships, not matching text.
Deliverable: hybrid, graph and agentic retrieval system with an ablation study, plus a text-to-SQL agent guarded against destructive queries.

modules.title: Month 4 — Memory Architecture & Multi-Agent Systems
points: Full memory taxonomy and lifecycle; consolidation, decay and forgetting policies; temporal knowledge graphs and bi-temporal facts.
Conflict detection and resolution; self-editing memory.
Procedural memory and skill libraries that agents write for themselves; experience replay and case-based reasoning.
Memory evaluation methodology; retention, residency and right-to-erasure engineering.
Topology selection and coordination theory; typed inter-agent contracts; blackboard and shared-workspace designs.
Market, auction and negotiation protocols; debate and adversarial verification.
The Agent2Agent protocol — agent cards, discovery, task lifecycle, streaming and cross-organisation agents.
Agent identity, authentication and delegated authorisation; failure modes including cascading errors, context contamination, infinite handoff and cost explosion.

Tool stack: Letta · Zep · Graphiti · Mem0 · LangGraph Store · Neo4j · Redis · Presidio · A2A Protocol SDK · Google ADK · Microsoft Agent Framework · LangGraph multi-agent · Ray · Kafka · SPIFFE · SPIRE
Real use: a self-improving operations agent with reusable procedures, plus cross-company agent negotiation via published agent cards with structured task messages.
Deliverable: memory and skill-library architecture with a measured improvement curve, plus an A2A-compliant agent interoperating with a second organisation's agent and a failure-mode control matrix.

modules.title: Month 5 — Computer Use, Browser Fleets & Autonomous Coding
points: Vision-grounded versus DOM-grounded control; accessibility-tree action spaces; self-healing automation and drift detection.
Secure credential injection without exposing secrets to the model; isolated virtual desktops and egress control; legal and terms-of-service considerations.
Coding agents at scale — repository-level context, planning, test-driven loops, patch validation and multi-repo refactors; agent-in-CI review.
Tool stack: Playwright · Browser Use · Stagehand · Claude Code with subagents · OpenHands · E2B Desktop · HashiCorp Vault

Real use: fleet-scale legacy automation — hundreds of scheduled browser agents reconciling vendor portals nightly, with drift detection that opens a ticket when a portal's interface changes instead of silently producing wrong numbers.
Deliverable: hardened browser-agent fleet with vault-based credentials, drift alerts, and a coding agent that lands 5 reviewed pull requests in a real repository.

modules.title: Month 6 — Evaluation Science & Benchmarking
points: Eval as an engineering discipline; dataset design, stratification and leakage control; annotation workflows and inter-rater agreement.
Judge calibration, bias, position effects and confidence intervals; statistical significance for model comparisons.
Trajectory, tool-selection and partial-credit scoring; simulated users and environment-based evaluation; agentic benchmarks and their limits.
Online eval, shadow traffic and interleaving; continuous evaluation as a service.
Tool stack: Braintrust · LangSmith · Inspect AI · W&B Weave · Arize Phoenix · DeepEval · OpenTelemetry GenAI · ClickHouse

Real use: an evaluation platform as an internal product — ten product teams push their agents through one shared eval service with common metrics, so leadership can compare quality across the portfolio and block releases on evidence rather than opinion.
Deliverable: multi-tenant evaluation service with calibrated judges, significance testing, drift alarms and a portfolio quality dashboard.

modules.title: Month 7 — Security Architecture & Fine-Tuning
points: Threat modelling agents with STRIDE adapted for tool-using systems; the OWASP agentic threat taxonomy.
Indirect prompt-injection defence in depth — provenance tagging, content isolation, dual-LLM patterns, capability restriction, egress allow-lists and human confirmation for irreversible actions.
Data exfiltration channels; privilege escalation; multi-agent trust boundaries; MCP supply-chain security; sandbox escape.
Continuous automated red teaming; forensics from traces.
When post-training beats prompting and retrieval; dataset construction from production traces and rejection sampling; data quality, deduplication and contamination checks.
Supervised fine-tuning with LoRA and QLoRA against full fine-tuning trade-offs; tool-call and function-calling fine-tunes.
Distillation from a frontier teacher; hyperparameter and compute budgeting.
Catastrophic forgetting and regression suites; adapter serving and multi-LoRA hosting.

Tool stack: Garak · PyRIT · Lakera Guard · NeMo Guardrails · gVisor · Firecracker · Falco · Vault · Semgrep · Sigstore · Hugging Face TRL · PEFT · Unsloth · Axolotl · DeepSpeed · FSDP · vLLM multi-LoRA · Weights & Biases
Real use: the security sign-off package a CISO needs, plus a specialised in-house 7–14B model post-trained on your own tool schemas that outperforms a frontier model on your specific workflow.
Deliverable: complete security package (threat model, control matrix, red-team pipeline, incident runbook) plus an SFT-tuned agentic model beating the base model on a held-out tool-use benchmark.

modules.title: Month 8 — Reinforcement Learning & Voice/Multimodal Agents
points: Preference optimisation with DPO, KTO and ORPO and when each applies; reward models against verifiable rewards.
GRPO and policy-gradient training on tool-use tasks; environment and task design for agentic RL.
Reward hacking — how it appears and how to detect it; rollout infrastructure and sample efficiency; compute budgeting.
Self-improvement and rejection-sampling loops; evaluating an RL-trained agent honestly.
Real-time voice pipelines — voice activity detection, streaming speech-to-text, turn detection, barge-in, text-to-speech and end-to-end speech models.
Latency budgeting for a sub-800 millisecond conversational feel; telephony integration and call transfer to humans.
Vision agents over documents, screenshots, charts and video; multimodal RAG; OCR-free document understanding.
Accessibility and quality evaluation for speech.

Real use: verifiable-reward tool-use training lifting tool-call accuracy, plus a voice front line — an inbound phone agent that verifies identity, resolves routine requests and hands off to a human when needed.

Deliverable: preference- or GRPO-trained checkpoint with benchmark gains, plus a production voice agent with under 900 millisecond turn latency, barge-in, warm human handoff and a 50-call evaluation report.

modules.title: Month 9 — Agent Platform Design, Governance & Capstone
points: Reference architecture for an internal agent platform — control plane, data plane, gateway, registry, eval service and observability.
Stateful scaling and session affinity; multi-region and disaster recovery; sandbox fleets and warm pools; multi-tenancy and isolation; semantic caching.
Capacity planning and load shedding; golden paths and self-service developer experience; versioning prompts, tools, models and graphs together.
Eval gates, canary rollout and automatic rollback; on-call for agents; cost per successful task, budget enforcement and chargeback.
Risk classification and the autonomy ladder — from suggest, to approve, to act with review, to act autonomously.
EU AI Act obligations, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001; sector rules including GDPR, DPDP, HIPAA, PCI-DSS and SOC 2.
Data residency and retention; auditability and decision logging; human oversight design; bias and fairness testing; model and system cards; vendor assessment.

Real use: choose one platform-scale build — a multi-tenant agent platform for a mid-size enterprise; an autonomous financial analysis system with a full audit trail; a clinical operations agent network with HIPAA-grade controls; a supply-chain multi-agent optimisation; or an autonomous site reliability platform with tiered human oversight.
